text: MEASURED BY THE CHIEF FROM BYTECODE, not from source reading: 84 case classes in the repo declare a private or private-scoped constructor; 80 expose a public fromProduct (javap on every companion); 45 of those 80 guard a real validating smart constructor returning Either or Option, so fromProduct is a working bypass of the validation the type certifies. Twelve modules. Includes StorySource, ValidatedVector, EmbeddingReceipt, ItemDigest, CacheKey, Credence, Coverage, SpanSet, TokenRange, AlignmentMatrix, AlignmentRow, HsmmConfig, CostWeights, EpisodeModel, Distribution, MentionGraph, Projection and eleven view types. NOT A LIVE WRONG ANSWER: zero calls to fromProduct exist in production or test code, and no internal path reaches it accidentally. It is a boundary-integrity defect - a library invariant that holds only for well-behaved callers is a convention, not an invariant. FIX IS UNBLOCKED: repo-wide there are 6 occurrences of 'derives' and 2 of 'Mirror' and ALL EIGHT ARE PROSE IN DOC COMMENTS - no typeclass derivation, no Mirror summoning - so converting a validating case class to a final class with explicit accessors, structural equals/hashCode and an intentional toString breaks no derivation. Same shape already required for Conditional. SEQUENCING: the engineer's PopulationAggregate change in bd-01M15XZ290HDMPTA4NXP88G4CM is the REFERENCE SHAPE and must land first; then module-sized slices, no slice mixing modules, ordered privacy/identity first (StorySource, EmbeddingReceipt, ItemDigest, CacheKey, ValidatedVector), then estimand carriers (Coverage, Credence), then the rest.
